analysis: Examined the two supplied base_text units of ClusterOnboardingFlow.swift (base lines 486-1379). The visible code is onboarding UI/advice logic: ClusterOnboardingMode.automaticIndex, ClusterOnboardingModeAdvice.advise, ClusterOnboardingDeployment text helpers, provisioning offer, update/version-split helpers, ready-line formatting and ClusterOnboardingSync. It handles no keys, attestation, encryption or authorization decisions. The patch excerpt is truncated (patch_excerpt_complete=false) and the changed ranges lie mostly outside the supplied base text (base changes begin at line 2844). The visible hunk adds two closure properties on the operations struct, `stopsAsked` and `serveUnlessStopped`, and passes `stopsBefore: nil` to provision(...). Those are behavior-bearing, but their implementations (stop-count under lock, stop-vs-start race, live operations) are not in the supplied units. Head-side changes (1518-1525, 2901-3013, 3316-3335, 3518-3539) were not visible, so I cannot assess them. Defensive input handling in the visible code looks sound: shownPlainly strips control characters for remote or catalog text, with length caps in shownMarker and recorded. The version-split and pinned-digest logic fail closed when the digests are unknown or differ (oneBuild, changed, memberWaitsForLeaderSetup). Relevant context is mainly the stop/serve race (a stop being undone by a concurrent start), which touches cluster-lifecycle availability; no explicit threat ID covers it. The next pass should examine the head-side implementation of serveUnlessStopped and stopsAsked, and the live callers that supply stopsBefore, to confirm a stop cannot be undone and that the lock covers the check. No findings are supported by the visible evidence. This is a coverage limit, not a clearance of the unseen changed regions.
